# HDT test fixtures

Byte-real `.hdt` (Header-Dictionary-Triples) container files for the
HDT reader track
([`docs/designissues/2026-07-06-hdt-program-plan.md`](../../../docs/designissues/2026-07-06-hdt-program-plan.md)),
generated by the **reference implementation** (hdt-cpp 1.3.3) from RDF
files already vendored in this repository, so every fixture has a
known ground-truth triple set parseable by the project's own verified
N-Triples parser.

## Provenance

- **Generator:** `HDTManager::generateHDT` + `HDT::saveToHDT` from
  hdt-cpp **1.3.3**, compiled from the sources vendored inside the
  [pyHDT](https://github.com/Callidon/pyHDT) 2.3 sdist on PyPI
  (`https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/51/82/41f1e4a131881da64a1ab2c4675dd93020a1a7109be08a2eb790cb6b92c6/hdt-2.3.tar.gz`,
  229,517 bytes, directory `hdt-cpp-1.3.3/`). Direct fetch of
  `github.com/rdfhdt/hdt-cpp` was unavailable through this sandbox's
  proxy (HTTP 403) at generation time (2026-07-06); the sdist carries
  the identical library sources. N-Triples front end: the reference
  `RDFParserSerd` against Ubuntu's `libserd-dev` 0.32.2.
- **Driver:** [`mini_rdf2hdt.cpp`](mini_rdf2hdt.cpp) (committed here),
  a ~30-line main() over the reference API. Build + regenerate:

  ```
  pip download hdt==2.3 --no-deps --no-binary :all:  # or the URL above
  tar xzf hdt-2.3.tar.gz && cd hdt-2.3
  apt-get install libserd-dev
  g++ -O1 -std=c++11 -w -include cstdint -include cstddef -DHAVE_SERD \
      -I/usr/include/serd-0 \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libhdt/include -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libhdt/src/dictionary \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libhdt/src/sparql -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/include \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/static/bitsequence \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/static/coders \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/static/mapper \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/static/permutation \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/static/sequence \
      -Ihdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src/utils \
      $(find hdt-cpp-1.3.3/libcds/src hdt-cpp-1.3.3/libhdt/src -name '*.cpp') \
      ../mini_rdf2hdt.cpp -lserd-0 -o mini_rdf2hdt
  ./mini_rdf2hdt <input.nt> <output.hdt> <baseURI>
  ```

- **License:** hdt-cpp is LGPL 2.1+ (per its source headers); pyHDT
  is MIT. The `.hdt` files here are *data produced by* those tools
  from inputs whose licenses govern the content: the RML ontology is
  CC-BY 4.0 (kg-construct), the W3C rdf-tests file is under the W3C
  Test Suite License. `mini_rdf2hdt.cpp` (this repo's driver) links
  against LGPL sources at build time only; it is not shipped as a
  binary.

| `rdf-mt-test002.hdt` | 2,040 | `c5442e54470b81cf6ae44d39f32e723110b9c3af622956229060f63fd2522868` | `third_party/testing/w3c/rdf/rdf11/rdf-mt/datatypes/test002.nt` | `http://example.org/` | 1 |

Expected stats, as written by the reference tool into each fixture's
own Header section (cross-checked by the stage-1 tests):

- `rml-core-ontology.hdt`: `void:triples` 343, `void:distinctSubjects`
  84, `void:distinctObjects` 173,
  `hdt:dictionarynumSharedSubjectObject` 39, `hdt:originalSize` 44159,
  `hdt:hdtSize` 8102, triples order SPO, format
  `<http://purl.org/HDT/hdt#dictionaryFour>` /
  `<http://purl.org/HDT/hdt#triplesBitmap>`.
- `rdf-mt-test002.hdt`: `void:triples` 1.

## Known gaps / upgrade path

These fixtures are single-implementation (hdt-cpp 1.3.3 only). When
`github.com/rdfhdt/*` is reachable from a build environment, add: a
fixture from `rdfhdt/libhdt`'s `tests/` data and/or an
hdt-java-generated sibling of the same inputs, to pin
cross-implementation compatibility (tracked as a stage-2 acceptance
criterion in the program plan).
